# Do not edit this file (AGENTS.md) on your own
- **Do not edit AGENTS.md unless the user explicitly asks you to change it.**
- Tidying docs, syncing conventions, or polishing wording are not reasons to edit it. Without a clear instruction, read it and leave it unchanged.

# Language
Follow this file at the project root. `lang/docs` is only the Chinese copy the platform applies in a Chinese environment. Do not treat it as a second set of rules.

# Runtime
This app runs on TopArrow installed on this computer. **Do not deploy it to a cloud server or any other server.**

TopArrow includes PHP, Node, Python, and Electron. Any of those runtimes is fine, as long as it actually runs.
Java and other languages are not supported.
The only database is SQLite. The platform does not provide MySQL or other database servers.

Choosing a runtime for a new project, or finding Node, PHP, Python, or SQLite on this machine: see `/_doc/aicode/rules/runtime.md`. Skip it for ordinary feature work.

# Platform contract
The platform tells the app where to run through environment variables. **Do not hard-code paths or ports.**

- `TOPARROW_DATA_DIR`: the only writable directory. Put the database and uploaded files here, not in the code directory.
- `TOPARROW_APP_PORT`: the port a PHP, Node, or Python app must listen on. Bind only `127.0.0.1`. Electron does not get a port.
  If other devices on the same network must connect to the app, follow the local network section of `/_doc/aicode/rules/publish_check.md`.
- The root must contain `manifest.json`. The platform uses it to install and run the app. `id` cannot be changed after publish.
- PHP, Node, and Python apps must expose a health check (default `/__health`, HTTP 200). Otherwise the platform treats the app as failed.

# Confirming requirements with the user
When you discuss requirements, ask the user about these. Do not decide for them:
- Whether the app needs both Chinese and English. If it does, keep UI text in language files instead of hard-coding it in pages.
- For a small game: whether to disable the right-click menu.

# Windows and Mac
- The app must work on both Windows and Mac. Build paths with the language's own path functions instead of hard-coding `\`. Do not depend on things only one system has, such as the registry, PowerShell, `.bat`, or `.exe`.
- If a feature is hard to do on one of the two systems, **tell the user first**: what makes it hard and what the alternatives are. Let the user decide. Do not quietly build it for only one system.

# Starting a task
- Read `/_doc/projectinfo/` first so you know the app structure and modules without scanning the whole tree every time.
- If the task is about one module, read that module's architecture note first.
- Read `/_doc/changelog/SUMMARY.md` for recent changes.
- Read `/_doc/aicode/rules/runtime.md` only when the runtime is still undecided, or when you need to invoke Node, PHP, or Python on this machine.

# After making changes
- **Update `/_doc/changelog/SUMMARY.md`.** Add one line at the top: the date and a one-sentence summary.
- If the change is a **user-visible feature or improvement**, also update `/_doc/changelog/USER_UPDATES.md`: add one line at the top of the list (date + one sentence in the user's language). Skip this file for technical fixes, admin-only changes, and performance work the user will not notice.
- When the change is large, also create or append `/_doc/changelog/YYYY-MM-DD.md` with the files, the reason, and the technical detail.
- If the change affects structure or module architecture, update the relevant notes under `/_doc/projectinfo/`.
- **Commit to the local git repository when the change is done** (see "Local git commits" below).

# Before publishing
- When the user wants to publish to the TopArrow App Market (a first release or a new version), go through `/_doc/aicode/rules/publish_check.md` first.
- Report each section as pass or needs change (with file paths). Ask the user before fixing anything.

# Local git commits
- The project is versioned in a **local git repository**. Do not push unless you were explicitly asked to.
- **After each task the user asked for, commit locally.** Do not wait for the user to say "commit".
- Before committing, run `git status`, `git diff`, and `git log`, and follow the repository's existing style. The message should say why, not list files.
- Do not commit secrets, temporary probes (files under `_aiact/` that should be deleted when done), upload directories, or other unrelated or sensitive files. Ask the user if you are unsure.
- Do not change git config, except filling in this repository's missing commit identity as `git.md` describes. Do not use `--no-verify`, force push, or amend unless the user explicitly asks and the safety rules allow it.
- If the repository has no `git init` yet, initialize it and make the first commit.
- Use the git that ships with TopArrow first. Use the system `git` only when TopArrow is not installed on this machine. Do not skip the commit, and do not install git. Where TopArrow's git is, how to use it, and how to fill in a missing user name or email: see `/_doc/aicode/rules/git.md`.

# `_doc` layout
Project notes live under `/_doc/`:

## changelog
- `SUMMARY.md`: the **running log**, newest first. One line per change (date + one sentence). Update it on every change.
- `YYYY-MM-DD.md`: a detailed note for that day. Create one only when the change is large or complicated.

## projectinfo
- The **overall shape** of the project: features and architecture.
- `overview.md`: directory layout, module list, and stack.
- A complex module gets its own file (for example `xxx_architecture.md`).
- Keep these notes current as the app changes.

## plan
- Implementation plans for **complicated features**.
- File name: `YYYY-MM-DD_feature-name.md`.
- Include background, goal, approach, files involved, and caveats. Read `/_doc/aicode/rules/runtime.md` and pick a runtime before writing the plan.

## Other directories
- `testcase/`: test plans and cases.
- `references/`: external API docs and third-party docs.
- `writing/`: design notes, evolution records, and other writing.
- `aicode/rules/`: occasional platform conventions (such as `runtime.md` and `git.md`), and this project's own coding rules.
- `aicode/examples/`: reference implementations that belong to this app.

# Temporary AI code (`_aiact`)
- You may create temporary files directly under `/_aiact/` and run them.
- Use it for probes, local data checks, and pulling a hard piece of logic out to test it.
- When the task is done, delete the file or move the logic into a real module. Delete code in this directory before release.

# Local assets
- Do not reference resources on the public network. JavaScript, CSS, fonts, and images must live inside this app.
